title: B1c BUILD (live registry): migrate PR-001..PR-004 to schema v2 with sources backfilled from their real ORCHESTRATION.md origins
description: Migrate the four live seed records to schema v2 exactly as the synthesis's migration semantics fix, backfilling the new mandatory fields - above all `sources`, the interpretive resources that actually produced each decision (A1, addendum section 3: second-degree documents without their first-degree sources make founded overruling impossible). The four records and their origins: PR-001 reopen-terminal-state (issuing task T-302), PR-002 test-discovery-precision (T-057), PR-003 verbatim-promotion (T-057), PR-004 verifier-rotation (T-031). This task writes the LIVE registry, which is why content preservation is its acceptance test rather than a nicety: an in-place rewrite that loses a character of a published ratio is the layer breaking its own immutability rule while claiming to enforce it. Runs concurrently with T-354 (disjoint files) and with T-358 (disjoint record ids, guarded allocation).
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY: the four live records .harness/precedents/PR-001.json, PR-002.json, PR-003.json, PR-004.json; .harness/tests/test_precedent_migration.py (new file); and .harness/tests/test_precedent_seed.py (the 14 pre-existing seed tests assert v1 content and are yours to update). Acquire `python3 .harness/bin/lock.py acquire <path> --holder <you> --task T-355` on each. Do NOT edit .harness/bin/precedent.py (T-353 shipped it, T-354 may be editing it right now), do NOT publish any new record (T-358 mints PR-005 and higher), do NOT touch test_precedent.py, test_precedent_conflicts.py or test_precedent_force.py, do NOT edit .harness/precedents/README.md.

BACKFILL sources FROM REAL ORIGINS, NEVER FROM INVENTION. Each record's sources must name the interpretive resources that actually produced that decision - the ORCHESTRATION.md rule by section heading, the issuing task's recorded verdict, the P-number, the code path - and every token must satisfy the v2 citation grammar the synthesis fixed. A source you cannot point at is not a source: leave it out and say so explicitly in the handoff. Fabricated provenance on the layer's own founding records is the worst outcome available to this task.

CONTENT PRESERVATION IS THE ACCEPTANCE TEST. No migrated record may lose or alter a single character of: ratio, dicta, scope_conditions, declared_width, tier_evidence, cites, subject, title, issuing_task, published_by, published_at, authority_tier, confirmation_status, confirmed_by, confirmed_at. PROVE IT: dump the four records before migrating, migrate, then diff field by field and paste the complete diff in the handoff. Any change to an SDR-01 immutable field beyond the additive v2 fields and the schema_version bump is a REJECT of your own work. The pre-migration content is recoverable independently via `git show HEAD:.harness/precedents/PR-001.json` (all four are tracked) - the verifier will use that, so your diff must match it.

IDEMPOTENT AND GUARDED: the migration runs inside harness_common.guarded() and re-running it on already-v2 records is a NO-OP. Ship a test that runs it twice and asserts byte-identical output. This is not tidiness: T-358 mints new records into the same directory concurrently with this task, and guarded plus idempotent is exactly what makes that concurrency safe.

TOUCH NOTHING BUT THE FOUR: ship a test asserting that after your migration no file named PR-005 or higher exists as a result of your work and that .harness/precedents/README.md is unchanged. If T-358 has already run and PR-005+ exist, your migration must leave them untouched (they are born at v2) - assert that too.

State, per record, which environment facts the ratio presupposes (file paths, verb names, board mechanics, repo state) and leave them in the unconfirmed class exactly as the schema's class-W discipline requires. Do NOT silently promote any field to confirmed: you are the producer, and author-declared reach measures roughly 2x random against roughly 5x for benefit attribution (papers/agentic_harness_engineering.pdf:9 section 4.4.2), which is the whole reason the confirm lifecycle exists.
